witnesses.provenance: Solana's per-transaction MAX_COMPUTE_UNIT_LIMIT is 1,400,000 compute units. It is the chain's limit, not ours. The campaign sets ProgramTest's ceiling to exactly that value and never raises it.

A `wire_bytes` of null says the campaign did not measure, which is honest but is not a claim that the frame fits. This asserts that no transaction in this campaign is unmeasured -- which matters more here than usual, because two of them do not fit and the next witness is where that is written down.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.label | test("append observation 2|consumption")) | "\(.label)=\(.wire_bytes)"] | unique | sort | join(" + ")
witnesses.expect: relayed consumption: a sealed graduation resolves the market=733 + relayed consumption: a sealed mint-authority renunciation resolves the market=733 + relayed transport: append observation 2=1196
witnesses.provenance: Against Solana's 1,232-byte PACKET_DATA_BYTES. Consumption was 1,534 as a legacy message (+302) and the widest append 1,377 (+145); neither was submittable and ProgramTest submits no packet to say so. Both now execute as v0 messages over a table frozen for the route, derived from the route's own metas by the message compiler. The two are NOT the same kind of overrun and the figures are what shows it: consumption is key-heavy -- 27 of its 30 addresses become one-byte indexes and it lands at 733, half the maximum. The append is DATA-bound: only seven addresses are eligible (the relayer and worker sign, the ed25519 precompile and Resolution are invoked), so the table buys a constant 181 bytes on all four appends and observation 2 lands at 1,196 with 36 bytes of headroom. That is not a margin to plan on, and the lever if the chunk grows is the relay's own commit-don't-inline seam -- the append IS the chunk -- not a wider table.

The liveness walk is the one route in this family that has to work when nobody is cooperating, so it is the one that must not depend on an Address Lookup Table a silent operator might never have published. Its twenty-two-account frame serialises to 991 bytes against Solana's 1,232-byte legacy maximum -- it fits on a bare legacy message, and this checks that separately from the family's two over-limit transactions above. It stays LEGACY, and that is the point of keeping this witness separate from the packet-wide one: a route that has to run when nobody cooperated must not make table publication a liveness precondition. Every liveness transaction is 991 bytes on a plain legacy message, 241 under the maximum, and needs no table to exist.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.error != null) | select([.logs[] | select(contains("custom program error: 0x"))] | length == 0)] | length | tostring
witnesses.provenance: The Solana runtime reports a privilege, frame, or account refusal it decides ITSELF as a bare InstructionError with no `custom program error:` log line; that line appears only when a program returned ProgramError::Custom. Every refusal this campaign claims is a decision the Resolution program made on a named field, so a bare runtime refusal appearing here would mean a hostile case stopped being about the adapter.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.error == null) | select(.label | startswith("relayed liveness:") or startswith("relayed consumption:")) | ([.logs[] | select(test("^Program 11111111111111111111111111111111 invoke"))] | length)] | unique | join(",")
witnesses.provenance: The bounty must move by direct lamport assignment between accounts the Resolution program owns, not by a System transfer from whoever submitted the transaction -- otherwise a "prepaid" bounty is a subsidy from the walker's own payer, and the escrow the market funded at founding is decoration. What the adapter legitimately asks the System Program for is exactly two things, and only for the certificate account: `allocate` then `assign`, because the certificate arrives PREPAID and System-owned (initialize_certificate_at_kind refuses anything else) so there is nothing to fund. This asserts the walk makes exactly those two System invocations -- the SAME two the already-audited consumption route makes for the same prepaid-output shape, which is why both labels are in the query and the result is required to be a single value. A third would be a transfer. `11111111111111111111111111111111` is Solana's System Program address; its provenance is outside this repository.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.error == null) | .label | if test("create the observation record") then "CreateRecord" elif test("append observation") then "AppendObservation" elif test("seal the completed set") then "SealRecord" elif test("retire the record") then "RetireRecord" elif test("^relayed consumption:") then "ConsumeRecord" elif test("^relayed liveness:") then "CommitDeadlineFailure" else "UNMAPPED:\(.)" end] | unique | sort | join(" + ")
witnesses.expect: AppendObservation + CommitDeadlineFailure + ConsumeRecord + CreateRecord + RetireRecord + SealRecord
witnesses.provenance: The family's closed action set is `RelayActionV1`: CreateRecord, AppendObservation, SealRecord, RetireRecord, ConsumeRecord, CommitDeadlineFailure -- six variants, enumerated in crates/dclutch-relay-contract/src/instruction.rs. This asserts the campaign drives all six, by NAME rather than by counting labels. Counting labels was the earlier form and it was wrong: it read 6 because the campaign happened to have one label per action, and it went silently red at 871017cf when a second consumption market was added -- a seventh label for an action already covered. Nothing ran the runner between then and 2026-09-02, so nobody saw it. Naming the actions keeps the tripwire the count was for -- a route with no mapping here appears as `UNMAPPED:<label>` and turns this red -- while a second market for an action already driven no longer breaks it.

Against Solana's 1,232-byte PACKET_DATA_BYTES. Three transactions -- the widest append and both consumptions -- were over it before 2026-09-02. Nulls are excluded on purpose: an unmeasured transaction is not a transaction that fits, and `relayed-measured-every-transaction` is what holds that count at zero.
